extracted.intended_audience: book volume editors (including proceedings, encyclopedia, handbook and textbook editors)
extracted.subtask_short: book volume editor code of conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Code of conduct and best-practice standards for editors of scholarly book volumes, covering responsibilities from proposal submission and peer review to conflicts of interest, confidentiality, and handling errors or ethical transgressions. Intended to guide editors working with Springer Nature on edited volumes and similar book projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Springer Nature minimum standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should follow the minimum standards as set out in the Springer Nature Code of Conduct for Book Volume Editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching requirement: adhere to the publisher's Code of Conduct for Book Volume Editors (applies to proceedings, encyclopedias, handbooks, textbooks, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of submitted proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitted book proposal must be original and must not contain any plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision to move forward is decided by (peer) review of the proposal to establish its intended appeal to a certain audience as well as other considerations such as market potential, fit with the publishing portfolio in that specific field, related publications, previous experiences (amongst others). The Publisher may use software to screen for plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal evaluation considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions on moving forward are based on peer review of the proposal to establish intended appeal and other considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider market potential, fit with the publishing portfolio in the specific field, related publications, previous experiences, and intended audience when assessing a proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer suggestion/selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may suggest (or request to exclude) reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Publisher has sole discretion whether or not to use suggested or excluded reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organise and structure the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Organise and structure the work as a whole (when there are multiple book Editors it is understood that all contributed sufficiently to this process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple editors are listed, they should all have contributed sufficiently to organization and structure of the volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate contributing authors/contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the appropriate contributing Authors and / or Contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are responsible for choosing contributors whose work fits the volume and meets expected standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure contributors comply with author code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the contributing Authors (including the Editors, if they also serve as contributing Authors) are aware of and compliant with the expectations as set out in the Code of Conduct for Book Authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must communicate publisher expectations and ensure author compliance with the separate Authors' Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate and final list of contributors and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that the list of contributing Authors including who is acting as Corresponding Author (names, affiliations and sequence) as well as the Editor names, affiliations and sequence are correct and final when the manuscript is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the manuscript has been delivered to production, changes to Author- or Editorship are no longer possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critically review and accept responsibility for final manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Critically review, approve and accept responsibility for the final manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must take responsibility for the scholarly quality and integrity of the final work before submission/production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support publisher in resolving author issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the Publisher in clarifying any doubt or misunderstanding with contributing Authors in relation to any of the topics specified below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be available to assist the publisher in communications with contributors about ethics, authorship, corrections, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional and timely communication with publisher
rubrics_metrics.description: Deal with the Publisher and its staff in a professional and courteous manner, ensuring their communications are appropriate in both volume and tone, and address all queries received relating to the work in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professionalism in tone and frequency; respond promptly to publisher queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement and practice of peer review for contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature endorses (peer) review as a key factor in developing and validating high quality scholarly publications; the approach to assess the merit of a Contribution should be aligned with both the expectations of the intended audience and norms within a specific discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice is to solicit constructive feedback from an appropriate number of independent experts. Reviewers should be made aware of the expectations set out in the Guidelines for Book Reviewers. The decision to include a Contribution in the final work is the responsibility of the Editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and prior publication restrictions for contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitted work must not contain any plagiarism and should not have been published elsewhere in any form or language (unless exceptions apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include translations of an original work, permission granted for reuse, a 'revised edition' with some degree of change, or reuse allowed under the Publisher’s reuse policy. The Publisher may use software to screen for plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of related manuscripts under consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should inform the Publisher of related works under consideration for publication and provide details of these relevant works (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: involvement with a major reference work as well as developing an edited volume on a similar topic. This ensures transparency and allows for proper citation of the first reported work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are requested to disclose interests that are directly or indirectly related to the work submitted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure helps transparency and allows readers to judge potential bias. Interests may include but are not limited to funding (grants, salaries, equipment, reimbursements), employment, financial interests (stocks, shares, consultation fees, patents), and non-financial interests (professional interests, personal relationships, positions on boards, consulting, expert witness roles, mentoring relations). Disclosure is not implied to make such relationships inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to report fundamental errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors have an obligation to share with the Publisher any significant error or inaccuracy in the published work either discovered by themselves or of which they are informed by an Author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision on how to correct the literature depends on the nature of the error and will be made by the Publisher following Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) guidelines. Corrections may include erratum/corrigendum or retraction. A retraction note must provide transparency as to which parts of the work are impacted. The Publisher may watermark or remove electronic editions and may withdraw printed editions as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of certain communications and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should treat the following as confidential: correspondence with direct representatives from the Publisher about the contract and contractual details of the work; Contributions under review; Reviewers’ reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If asked for information (e.g., by hiring or promotion committees), editors should only share the project's current status: out for review or in press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to suspected transgression of ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should take ethical complaints concerning a published work seriously and cooperate with the Publisher in carrying out an investigation following COPE guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, after investigation, there are valid concerns, measures may include rejection of the work if under consideration; placement of erratum/corrigendum; retraction (with transparent explanation and possible watermarking or removal of electronic/printed editions); informing the Author’s (or Editor’s) institution; and including a notice of suspected transgression in bibliographic records. The accused will be contacted and given an opportunity to address the issue.
